Distribution of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic

Source: R/ks_distribution.R
ks_sf.Rd

Upper tail probability P(D_n >= d) of the one-sample, two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic D_n = sup |F_n(x) - F(x)| of a sample of size n from a continuous distribution.

Usage

ks_sf(d, n, exact = TRUE)

Arguments

d

Value(s) of the statistic, in [0, 1].

n

Sample size (a positive integer, recycled with d).

exact

TRUE (the default) for the exact distribution of D_n, as scipy.stats.kstwo; FALSE for the limiting Kolmogorov distribution of sqrt(n) D_n, as scipy.stats.kstwobign.

Value

The probabilities P(D_n >= d).

Details

The exact distribution is computed as Simard and L'Ecuyer (2011), with the same choices of method as scipy.stats.kstwo: Ruben-Gambino formulas at the ends of the support; for n <= 140 the Durbin matrix (n d^2 <= 0.754693), the Pomeranz recursion (n d^2 <= 4) or twice the one-sided Smirnov tail; for larger n twice the one-sided tail (n d^2 >= 2.2), the Durbin matrix (n d^1.5 <= 1.4, n <= 100000) or the Pelz-Good approximation. The one-sided tail is the Birnbaum-Tingey sum.

References

Simard, R. and L'Ecuyer, P. (2011). Computing the two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov distribution. Journal of Statistical Software, 39(11), 1-18. doi:10.18637/jss.v039.i11

Marsaglia, G., Tsang, W. W. and Wang, J. (2003). Evaluating Kolmogorov's distribution. Journal of Statistical Software, 8(18), 1-4. doi:10.18637/jss.v008.i18

Examples

ks_sf(0.1, 100)
#> [1] 0.2526928
ks_sf(0.1, 100, exact = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.2699997
# same as the p-value of ks.test()
x <- c(0.61, 0.29, 0.06, 0.59, -1.73, -0.74, 0.51, -0.56, 0.39, 1.64)
ks.test(x, "pnorm")$p.value
#> [1] 0.6213478
ks_sf(unname(ks.test(x, "pnorm")$statistic), 10)
#> [1] 0.6213478
